goal: Evaluate B7-H3 (CD276) as a therapeutic target in lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) and small cell lung cancer (SCLC) only: tumor biology rationale, genetic/functional support, expression specificity and safety liability, clinical precedence, and ranked modality options.

steps.task: Genetic evidence and tractability for CD276 in LUAD and SCLC: resolve exact disease IDs, query GWAS/L2G/QTL colocalization, target prioritisation and tractability. Interpret candidly given CD276 is not a classic genetically driven target.
CD276 expression across cell types in LUAD and SCLC tumors versus normal lung, plus normal-tissue expression relevant to on-target off-tumor toxicity. CELLxGENE Census only; no spatial/Visium.
DepMap CRISPR dependency of CD276 across LUAD and SCLC cell lines and selectivity versus other lineages; whether tumor cells depend on CD276 and whether expression is retained.
Pathway and protein-interaction context for CD276: Reactome/GO annotations, interaction partners, immune-checkpoint biology, and pathway-based on-target safety considerations.
Clinical precedence for B7-H3-directed agents in LUAD and SCLC: ClinicalTrials.gov trials, agents, phases, status, and reported outcomes; cBioPortal if relevant. Restrict disease scope to LUAD/SCLC.
Safety profile of B7-H3 targeting: target safety events, known B7-H3 drug warnings/adverse events, mouse phenotypes, pharmacogenomics, and on-target off-tumor risk in normal tissues.
CD276 target biology for modality selection: protein class, isoforms, subcellular localization, homologues, tractability, expression overview, and implications for ADC/bispecific/CAR modalities.

Rank the top modalities for B7-H3 in LUAD and SCLC (e.g., ADC, bispecific/T-cell engager, CAR-T, radioimmunotherapy), using target-biologist biology findings and the clinical trial landscape; assess feasibility, timeline, cost, differentiation.
Review all specialist outputs against the user query, checking scope (LUAD/SCLC only), data support, internal consistency, and whether conclusions follow. Flag gaps and overreach.
